title: 2D pattern printing workflow
content:
Hello CLO3D Team,

I would like to share some feedback and a small wishlist regarding the 2D pattern printing workflow in CLO3D.

I develop all my patterns directly in 3D, and CLO3D is my main tool. While the necessary 2D functions already exist, I find them a bit difficult to use for real production needs, so I often have to export patterns to another program just to prepare them for printing.

A few things that would make a big difference for me:

Text labels on pattern pieces:  
it would be great to have a normal, non-bold font and the ability to scale text proportionally to the size of each piece, so I can place several lines of information (name, size, notes) in a clean way.

Notches:  
although I can place them in CLO3D, they unfortunately do not appear when I export patterns to PDF or PLT.

Printable layout:  
I can arrange pieces in a layout, but I am not able to export this layout to a proper PDF for printing.

Grainline:  
for printing patterns, it would be very helpful if the grainline always stayed exactly as defined during pattern development, regardless of how the piece is rotated in the layout.

In an ideal workflow, I would love to be able to label pieces, place them into a print layout, and export everything to PDF with all text, notches, and grainlines displayed correctly — without needing external software.

Thank you very much for your great work on CLO3D and for considering this feedback.

Kind regards,  
Natalia
content_description: To provide user feedback and feature requests aimed at improving the 2D pattern printing workflow in CLO3D for a more seamless and production-ready experience.

title: Exporting and Importing Without Distorting Measurements
content:
I want to export CLO3D project files (.zprj) so that I can add pattern information in **Affinity Designer** (a vector drawing app), and then import them back into **CLO3D**.

Question 1) Which export format should I use to work in Affinity Designer?

After adding the pattern information in Affinity Designer, which format should I use to import the files back into CLO3D? (Maybe I continue to edit the patterns here)

My main concern is **preserving the original measurements** during the conversion process.

**Question 2)**

If the **User Settings → Unit System** is set to **centimeters** , but the **export unit** is set to **millimeters** , will the measurements remain accurate without any distortion?

Question 3) If I follow the method you recommend, will the measurements remain accurate during export and import (without distortion or scaling issues)?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: "If the User Settings → Unit System is set to centimeters, but the export unit is set to millimeters, will the measurements remain accurate without any distortion?" This will nto affect the measurements, they will remain accurate. For the question about the 3rd party program which is not our expertise, you will have to check which file types you can export out of CLO that is compatible with it (e.g. PDF for the pattern) and just try it out and see how it goes.
Reply 1: Thank you very much.
content_description: Purpose: This page guides users on exporting CLO3D project files for pattern editing in Affinity Designer and reimporting them back into CLO3D while preserving accurate measurements throughout the process.

title: Issues with Export/Import to DXF for Lectra Modaris and Gerber
content:
TL/DR: Suppliers can't open my DXF exports from the most recent CLO versions, the last version that works is ver. 2024.2.328 (February 26, 2025). That version also has various problems in the exports detailed below. Has anyone had success exporting DXFs for use in Lectra Modaris and Gerber? Please let me know if there are any import/export settings that I or my suppliers are missing that will help us. Thank you!

Full Post: I have been having issues with exporting to dxf, both AAMA and ASTM, for use in Gerber Accumark, Optitex, and Lectra Modaris programs with suppliers. These issues are present in the DXF exports from the most recent versions of CLO:

  * Gerber cannot open files exported from the latest CLO versions at all: issue with piece perimeter missing (screenshot below)

  * ![106187d2b19d4493b563e7c12eca7253](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/5d0dee24ec86494a83eaa92fc6626900/images/106187d2b19d4493b563e7c12eca7253Gerber_CLO_Import_Issue.jpg)

  * Optitex cannot open files exported from the latest CLO versions: issue with incorrect scale.

  * Lectra Modaris does not maintain pattern arrangement/marker from CLO file-- the pattern pieces are scattered around the user interface and not in the positions I placed them. 

  * Lectra Modaris shows all lines (cut lines, internal lines, baselines) as cut lines. 




The most recent previous version of CLO that I found that exported something these programs could open was ver. 2024.2.328 (February 26, 2025). The following issues are present in dxf exports from that version:

  * Missing, undersized, or duplicate Notches (not all notches in a file, seemingly at random).

  * Duplicate internal/baselines in DXF exports-- these duplicate both the existing internal lines, AND there are additional internal/baselines copying the cut lines on all shapes. The files I am using are not meant to have seam allowance or grading, just cut lines and internal lines, and sometimes some baselines. 

  * Lectra Modaris does not maintain pattern arrangement/marker from CLO file-- the pattern pieces are scattered around the user interface and not in the positions I placed them. 

  * Lectra Modaris shows all lines (cut lines, internal lines, baselines) as cut lines. 




Please let me know if there is anything I can do on my end when exporting or anything my suppliers could easily do on their end for importing that would mitigate some of these issues. Thank you all!

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi there, we're sorry about the inconvenience! Please share an affected DXF to tech support so they can determine the cause: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/5d0dee24ec86494a83eaa92fc6626900 I can find no current reports of this extent so it it doesn't appear to be a systemic issue.
content_description: A collaborative forum post seeking solutions to DXF export issues from recent CLO versions for compatibility with Gerber, Optitex, and Lectra Modaris software.

title: Aligning And Saving Annotation Presets
content:
Aligning And Saving Annotation Presets

Question 1) How to align the annotation in the quickest way?

Like In the middle of the selected pattern. (Both vertical and horizontal.)

Can we do this automatically?

Question 2) How to add my brands icon onto the Annotation?

Question 3) I want to create a Annotation Preset in a particular Font, Font Size, Color and including my brands icon to use It on the every pattern I created.

How can I do this?  
Which file format etc.?

How can I import It on the project I work on?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, it is only possible to change color, font size and angle, as well as dragging and dropping to another position. But we can add a feature request for font type and measured positioning such as centering, etc. If you want to add your brand's icon, you can do this with an image file by placing it as a graphic (the official CONNECT store also has a logo on the patterns). There are no presets that can be saved and reused for annotating.
Reply 1: Understood. Thank you very much.
content_description: This page provides step-by-step guidance on quickly aligning annotations, adding brand icons, and creating reusable annotation presets with custom fonts and colors for seamless project integration.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Tina, two possible solutions: (1) Select the seamlines in questions and make their Normal Map "shadow" wider and/or more intense. (2) In the render window, select the render properties and edit the Global Map for seam puckering to be more intense. This will affect all seamlines.
